scenario.title: Atlas of Questions
scenario.premise: You are assembling a traveling atlas of how people make, challenge and share knowledge. Visit reconstructed workshops and documentary collections, then use their methods on openly speculative future problems. This is a thematic journey, not a claim that history followed one inevitable ladder. Historical people are not simulated speakers; all requests come from fictional curators.

stage.title: Who owns the night?
stage.speaker: Settlement grower and observatory keeper
stage.motivation: An orbital mirror could give our crops more light, but our neighbors need darkness. Make a shared-sky proposal and a pilot record that distinguishes switching the mirror off from undoing its effects.
stage.travelText: We collect the tools this collection needs from the places we have already visited. Everything else stays where we left it.

areas.label: Greenwich and the ship’s chart table
A comparative East Asian printing workshop

things.label: Open restitution case
things.description: The restitution case remains open beside a qualified reconstruction. Descendants gain a way to contest erasure, but the archive cannot manufacture the unknowable event that would settle every claim.

things.label: Mirror orbit
things.description: A fictional orbital-reflector proposal; its ability to provide useful crop lighting remains a model assumption.

things.label: Seasonal crop model
things.description: A fictional model relating the timing of extra light to growth, with other requirements still unresolved.

things.label: Water budget
things.description: A finite water constraint that limits the promised harvest benefit in the speculative case.

things.label: Night-sky survey
things.description: Records of darkness needed for a neighboring observatory's measurements.

things.label: Mirror schedule
things.description: The proposed timing of reflected illumination, which overlaps some dark-time activities.

things.label: Nocturnal habitat record
things.description: Evidence about ecological uses of darkness that a crop-yield calculation leaves out.

things.label: Alternative orbit
things.description: A modeled alternative reducing reflected light and some benefits as well as some harms.

things.label: Shutter control
things.description: A fictional actuator that stops further reflection, not a time machine undoing prior effects.

things.label: Long-term effects register
things.description: A record separating immediate operation from ecological and social consequences that might persist.

things.label: Extended-light forecast
things.description: In the fictional model, a mirror schedule adds light during part of the growing season. Extra light is only a proposed benefit: crops also depend on heat, water and biological responses.

things.label: Lost observing window
things.description: The schedule overlaps a neighboring observatory's dark-time window. The same reflected light is a resource for one group and lost observing capacity for another.

things.label: Conditional harvest forecast
things.description: The water budget limits the modeled harvest gain. A brighter field is not automatically a larger sustainable harvest, and the forecast is explicitly conditional.

things.label: Darkness-impact map
things.description: The habitat record expands the dispute beyond people and telescopes. Darkness has ecological roles that a simple crop-yield total would leave out.

things.label: Lower-light plan
things.description: An alternative orbit reduces the illumination and the predicted crop benefit. This is a concrete compromise, not a discovery of a free solution that satisfies everyone.

things.label: Shared-sky proposal
things.description: The proposal displays harvest limits beside observing and habitat losses. Different communities can reasonably weigh those outcomes differently; the artifact makes the disagreement legible.

things.label: Stoppable pilot
things.description: The fictional shutter can halt further illumination. Stoppable operation is a technical control, not proof that earlier ecological or social effects can be reversed.

things.label: Irreversible-risk record
things.description: The record separates what stops immediately from changes that may persist. It rejects the tempting equation 'off switch equals no lasting harm.'

things.label: Living atlas of consequences
things.description: The memory dispute and mirror dispute enter one atlas: new powers can illuminate lost places or dark fields while changing whose evidence, rights and environment count. The shared achievement is a contestable account of consequences, not unanimous progress.

cacheNarrative.label: An experiment we cannot undo: collection
cacheNarrative.narrative: Fictional orbital and crop models meet observing records, a water budget and testimony about the night. No actual deployment is proposed.
